title: Refactor Day Planner
story: Your morning schedule is a mess — wake up, eat, code, eat, gym, eat, sleep, all crammed into one giant block of scribbles. Time to organize your day into clean, reusable sections.
why: Refactoring a large main function into smaller named functions makes code readable, testable, and maintainable.
analogy: Think of your day planner like a filing cabinet. Instead of throwing all your papers into one big drawer, you sort them into labeled folders: Morning, Afternoon, Evening. When you need to find something, you go straight to the right folder.
try_it: Add a fourth function called `night_owl_mode()` that prints activities from 11 PM to 2 AM, and call it after `evening_routine()`.
tips: Each function should do ONE thing — morning, afternoon, or evening
Name functions after what they represent, not what they print
Calling order in main() determines execution order
Refactoring doesn't change what the program does, only how it's organized
common_mistakes: Putting all the code back into main() and forgetting to call the functions
Creating functions but never calling them from main()
Naming functions vaguely like `section1()`, `section2()` instead of descriptive names
